hunks.baseline: Hearing that familiar voice tremble with agitation, I let out the breath I’d been holding.
hunks.sol: Hearing that familiar voice tremble with emotion, I let out the breath I’d been holding.

hunks.baseline: I slowly blinked and swallowed the blood pooled in my mouth.
hunks.sol: I blinked slowly and swallowed the blood pooled in my mouth.

hunks.baseline: I felt hazy, as if I were trapped in a dream I could never escape. And yet, at the same time, everything around me came through with perfect clarity.
hunks.sol: I felt hazy, as though I were trapped in a dream I could never escape. Yet everything around me came through with startling clarity.

hunks.baseline: As for what this unfamiliar sensation was—the first I’d ever experienced—the System gave me a clear answer, as it always did.
hunks.sol: As for what this unfamiliar sensation was, the System gave me a clear answer, as it always did.

hunks.baseline: In its uniquely kind and cruel way.
hunks.sol: In its own unfailingly kind and cruel way.

hunks.baseline: Like the sunlight that blazes just before the sun sets, the last flame burning at the edge of a life fading into darkness.
hunks.sol: Like sunlight blazing just before sunset, it was the last flame to burn at the darkening edge of a life.

hunks.baseline: The thought came to me suddenly.
I remembered the final moments of all those people I’d personally brought down with these two hands—or desperately tried to hold on to, only to watch them leave anyway.
hunks.sol: I thought of the final moments of those I’d brought down with my own two hands—and those I’d desperately tried to hold on to, only to lose them anyway.

hunks.baseline: All the countless emotions I’d glimpsed in them.
hunks.sol: Of all the emotions I’d glimpsed in them.

hunks.baseline: At last, I felt like I could understand it all.
hunks.sol: At last, I felt as though I could understand them all.

hunks.baseline: And I understood something else, too: unlike them, who’d waited for death as it slowly drew near, I was the kind of fool who had no choice but to run straight toward it.
hunks.sol: I understood something else, too. Unlike them, who had waited for death as it slowly drew near, I was the kind of fool who had no choice but to run toward it.

hunks.baseline:
> **System**
>
> Final Rally is an act of divine mercy, a testament to human will, and a candle by which you may reflect on the life you have lived. Though its flame burns only briefly, that instant of light will shine so brightly that even death may be forgotten.
hunks.sol:
> **System**
>
> Final Rally is an act of divine mercy, an expression of human will, and a candle by which you may reflect on the life you have lived. Though its flame burns only briefly, that moment of light will shine so brightly that even death may be forgotten.

hunks.baseline: A clear chime, so familiar it rang in my ears, roused my body and mind from their endless plunge into darkness.
hunks.sol: A familiar, clear chime rang in my ears, rousing my body and mind from their endless plunge into darkness.

hunks.baseline: The radiant light the System had promised—a light bright enough to make me forget even death.
hunks.sol: Just as the System had said, it was a light bright enough to make me forget even death.

hunks.baseline: The trembling of my body, groaning under the pain and death closing in by the second, came to a halt.
hunks.sol: My body stopped trembling under the pain and death closing in by the second.

hunks.baseline:

hunks.sol:

hunks.baseline: A sudden warmth pierced my back. The spark swelled into a flame.
hunks.sol: Sudden warmth seeped into my back, and the spark swelled into a flame.

hunks.baseline: Someday they would clash and destroy each other.
hunks.sol: Sooner or later, they would collide and destroy each other.

hunks.baseline: But if they sprang from the same root, then they were originally one and the same.
hunks.sol: But if they came from the same root, they were one flame to begin with.

hunks.baseline: Just like the person who, despite suffering severe Internal Injuries of his own, had given me his energy without hesitation.
hunks.sol: Just like the person who, despite suffering severe Internal Injuries of his own, had shared his qi with me without hesitation.

hunks.baseline: His face was as pale as paper. Great and small wounds were etched across his body, and his frame trembled.
hunks.sol: His face was as pale as paper. Wounds large and small covered his body, and his frame trembled.

hunks.baseline: But he—Jeok Cheongang—was smiling at me.
hunks.sol: But Jeok Cheongang was smiling at me.

hunks.baseline: Trying to suppress the joy that his Disciple had recovered a little strength, along with the sorrow of what that meant.
hunks.sol: He was trying to hold back both his joy that his Disciple had regained a little strength and his sorrow at what that meant.

hunks.baseline: As time, which had stood still, began to flow again, I gripped White Flame tightly and took a step forward.
hunks.sol: Time began to flow again. I gripped White Flame tightly and took a step forward.

hunks.baseline: If this had been a fight I had to face alone, I might have given up already.
hunks.sol: If this had been my fight alone, I might have given up already.

hunks.baseline: I might have leaned my exhausted body against a pile of corpses, looked back on the time I’d left behind, and waited for death to slowly descend.
hunks.sol: I might have leaned my exhausted body against a pile of corpses, looked back on my life, and waited for death to descend.

hunks.baseline: Amid the reddish, overheated earth and the shimmering haze that warped the air, a giant of fire roared.
hunks.sol: Amid the reddish glow of the earth and the heat haze warping the air, a giant of fire roared.

hunks.baseline: At the same time, the Slaughter Saint, the Bow Saint, Cheongpung, and the last of the devoted defenders—
hunks.sol: At the same time, the Slaughter Saint, the Bow Saint, Cheongpung, and the last of the devoted defenders advanced.

hunks.baseline: And countless civilians beyond counting, surging behind them like a wave.
Their cries were no longer angry shouts. They were shouting the name of someone none of us had expected.
hunks.sol: Countless civilians followed behind them like a wave, no longer shouting out of desperation but calling a name none of us had expected.

hunks.baseline: The great shout shook the battlefield and reached my ears. A streak of lightning shot up my spine.
hunks.sol: The great shout shook the battlefield and reached my ears. A jolt like lightning shot up my spine.

hunks.baseline: Those people, who didn’t have a scrap of internal energy or a proper weapon, who held sickles and pickaxes in their hands.
hunks.sol: Those people with neither a scrap of internal energy nor a proper weapon, gripping sickles and pickaxes in their hands.

hunks.baseline: As the beloved faces I would never see again flashed through my mind, I shot toward the fanatics.
hunks.sol: The beloved faces I would never see again flashed through my mind, and I shot toward the fanatics.

hunks.baseline: The toes of my feet. My waist. My shoulder. My arms and wrists.
hunks.sol: My toes. My waist. My shoulder. My arms and wrists.

hunks.baseline: Following movements etched into instinct through countless repetitions and real battles, I split the raging wind and rain.
hunks.sol: My body followed movements etched into instinct through countless repetitions and real battles, splitting the raging wind and rain.

hunks.baseline: A single, cool cutting sound swept through the air.
hunks.sol: A single, cool cutting sound crossed the air.

hunks.baseline: The fanatics stared at me in disbelief, clutching their severed throats as they crumpled to the ground.
hunks.sol: The fanatics stared at me in disbelief, clutching their slit throats as they crumpled to the ground.

hunks.baseline: White Flame’s spearhead, trailing a faint heat, was slower and weaker than it had ever been. But for some reason, the enemies waiting in its path couldn’t react in time.
hunks.sol: White Flame’s spearhead, trailing faint heat, was far slower and weaker than usual. Yet for some reason, the enemies in its path couldn’t react.

hunks.baseline: And neither could the next wave, surging in to fill the gaps left by their dead comrades.
hunks.sol: Neither could those surging forward to fill the gaps left by their dead comrades.

hunks.baseline: A pair of fierce eyes, and the willow-leaf saber he always carried in his arms.
hunks.sol: A pair of fierce eyes, and the willow-leaf saber he always kept close.

hunks.baseline: But despite his appearance, Song Ilseom had always been a reliable comrade and a good person to me.
hunks.sol: But despite his rough appearance, Song Ilseom had always been a reliable comrade and a good person to me.

hunks.baseline: He complained every time about how dangerous the missions were and how much extra pay he deserved, but Song Ilseom always fought in the most dangerous places.
hunks.sol: He complained about the danger and the extra pay on every mission, yet he always fought in the most dangerous places.

hunks.baseline: *He must have. If it was the guy I knew.*
hunks.sol: *He must have. The Song Ilseom I knew would have.*

hunks.baseline: That was true of a wandering martial artist others might have seen as nothing but rough and uncouth. It was true, too, of the two unorthodox faction members I’d unexpectedly formed ties with.
hunks.sol: That was true of a wandering martial artist others might have seen as nothing but rough and uncouth. It was true, too, of the two members of the unorthodox faction I’d unexpectedly come to know.

hunks.baseline: Every word had been the truth. Not a trace of a lie in it.

hunks.sol: The words echoed endlessly somewhere deep inside me, and I moved as if entranced.

hunks.baseline: Like Sama Pyo, I cut off my enemies’ breath with the cruelest, surest methods.
hunks.sol: Like Sama Pyo, I ended my enemies’ lives by the cruelest, surest means.

hunks.baseline: Listening to voices that rang like hallucinations amid flying screams and blood.
hunks.sol: Voices rang like hallucinations amid flying blood and screams.

hunks.baseline: Seeing familiar faces laid over the enemies collapsing like bundles of straw.
hunks.sol: Familiar faces appeared, one after another, over the enemies collapsing like bundles of straw.

hunks.baseline: They rose like mist and passed like the wind.
hunks.sol: The memories rose like mist and passed like wind.

hunks.baseline: The Fire Courtyard of the Yongbong Escort Bureau, shrouded in deep darkness, and the full moon, unusually bright and large that night.
hunks.sol: The Fire Courtyard of the Yongbong Escort Bureau, shrouded in darkness, and the full moon, unusually bright and large that night.

hunks.baseline: The light, lively voice and the graceful, dancing steps, as if buoyed by drink.
hunks.sol: Her lively voice and light, dancing steps, buoyed by drink.

hunks.baseline: And the tearful eyes she couldn’t hide, no matter what she did.
hunks.sol: And the tears in her eyes that none of it could hide.

hunks.baseline: I remembered it all, vividly.
hunks.sol: I remembered it all vividly.

hunks.baseline: Even when I made a pointless fuss about how bright the moon was that night, then fell silent at her unexpected question.
hunks.sol: How I’d made a pointless fuss about the brightness of the moon, then fallen silent at her unexpected question.

hunks.baseline: Even the moment I looked into her eyes, brimming with tears, and opened my mouth.
hunks.sol: Even the moment I’d looked into her tear-filled eyes and spoken.

hunks.baseline: *“It’s all right if you can’t do it well. You don’t have to force yourself.”*
hunks.sol: *“It’s all right if you don’t do it well. You don’t have to try so hard.”*

hunks.baseline: Never imagining that a day like today would come, like the pitch-black Force rushing toward me right now.
hunks.sol: I’d never imagined a day like today would come—or that pitch-black Force would come rushing toward me as it was now.

hunks.baseline: More precisely, I didn’t have enough reason left to do so.

hunks.sol: I only faced the two streams of energy darkening my already hazy vision. They were so murky they hardly seemed alive at all.

hunks.baseline: And at the same time, in the gap between moments slowed to a crawl, I thrust out my spear.
hunks.sol: And in the gap between moments slowed to a crawl, I thrust out my spear.

hunks.sol: The only word for what had just happened was *shattering*.

hunks.baseline: Something so mysterious that even I, who had caused it, couldn’t understand.
hunks.sol: It was so inexplicable that even I, the one who’d done it, couldn’t understand it.

hunks.baseline: So perfectly shattered that it enraged even the dead who had just fired Force at me.
hunks.sol: So complete that it enraged even the dead who had fired that Force at me.

hunks.baseline: The two Black Ghosts still standing cried out in unison and charged.
hunks.sol: The last two Black Ghosts cried out in unison and charged.

hunks.sol: A ghostly horse crossed a dozen or so jang of open air in an instant, casting its shadow over me. Blood-red eyes flashed, and a still larger mass of Force slashed down.

hunks.baseline: The blast was so violent it shook my eardrums, already burst.
hunks.sol: The rushing blast was violent enough to shake even my already-burst eardrums.

hunks.baseline: But I wasn’t the only one waiting where they were headed.
hunks.sol: But I wasn’t the only one in its path.

hunks.baseline: In the blink of an eye, four streaks of light collided in midair and swelled.
hunks.sol: In the blink of an eye, four streaks of light tangled in midair and swelled.

hunks.baseline: The compressed air exploded, and the earth overturned, unable to withstand the tremendous force.
hunks.sol: The compressed air exploded, and the earth overturned beneath the tremendous force.

hunks.baseline: At the heart of it were two superhumans who’d rushed to save me.
hunks.sol: At the heart of it were two superhumans who had rushed to save me.

hunks.baseline: The Slaughter Saint’s short knife and ox-hair needles, and the two curved swords clenched in the Bow Saint’s hands, stabbed and sliced through the Black Ghosts at lightning speed.
hunks.sol: The Slaughter Saint’s short knife and ox-hair needles, and the two curved swords clenched in the Bow Saint’s hands, pierced and sliced through the Black Ghosts at lightning speed.

hunks.baseline: But unlike the Black Ghosts, the two Saints gritted their teeth, faces ashen, forcing out what little strength they had left.
hunks.sol: The two Saints gritted their teeth, faces ashen, wringing out what little strength they had left. The Black Ghosts, meanwhile, refused to fall.

hunks.sol: Enough to face two of the Three Saints, who had fought more fiercely than anyone and were now closer to their limits than anyone else.

I thought of a promise to one person that could never be kept now.

hunks.baseline: About the me who hadn’t been able to tell someone who’d become the greatest memory in the world to run away.
hunks.sol: Of the moment I hadn’t been able to bring myself to tell someone who had become my greatest memory in this world to run away.

hunks.baseline: Our first meeting had been a stubborn feud.
hunks.sol: We’d met as enemies who couldn’t seem to shake each other.

hunks.baseline: Before long, the two of us had fallen into step together.
hunks.sol: Before long, the two of us had fallen into step.

hunks.baseline: And then we’d become inseparable.
hunks.sol: Then we’d become inseparable.

hunks.baseline: So close that, at some point, we couldn’t even bear to be apart.
hunks.sol: So close that, at some point, being apart no longer felt right.

hunks.baseline: When I couldn’t see him, I missed him. When he was away, I worried about him.
hunks.sol: I missed him when I couldn’t see him, and worried when I sent him away.

hunks.baseline: In the end, I hadn’t even seen where or who had killed him.
hunks.sol: In the end, I hadn’t even seen where he’d died or who had killed him.

hunks.baseline: *Even if he somehow survived by some miracle, I’ll never see him again.*
hunks.sol: *Even if some miracle saved him, I’ll never see him again.*

hunks.baseline: Because I would die first.
hunks.sol: I would die before it could be.

hunks.sol: I would have to leave behind the people I’d wanted to protect—and those who might be waiting desperately for me somewhere—and set off down a long road from which there was no return.

hunks.baseline: I swung my spear, tirelessly rekindling the dying flame.
hunks.sol: I swung my spear, rekindling the dying flame without pause.

hunks.baseline: Trampling the corpses piling up with each step and the blood spurting into the air, I moved as one with the people protecting me.
hunks.sol: Trampling the corpses piling up with every step and the blood spurting beneath my feet, I moved as one with the people protecting me.

hunks.baseline: Toward the last and only path left to the living and the dead.
hunks.sol: Toward the last, the only path left for the living and the dead alike.

hunks.baseline: Toward the blood-red eyes I could sense with perfect clarity, even through my hazy vision.
hunks.sol: Toward the blood-red eyes I could sense clearly even through my hazy vision.

hunks.baseline: Beyond the fierce storm of blood, a monster steeped in blood and madness stood waiting.
hunks.sol: Beyond that fierce storm of blood stood a monster steeped in blood and madness.

hunks.sol: “You should be running for your life, yet you’ve come to me of your own accord. I hardly know how to thank you.”
